content.comment_body: Good evening, I would like some assistance with using [product_name] and the [product_name] library. Although the connection works, I encounter issues when trying to read certain fields. For example, I can only read the parameter M1.0 if I input it as M0.0, and similarly, M2 becomes M0.1, etc. Additionally, I haven't found a way to read VM-type variables. Any advice would be welcome. Thanks in advance, [user_name]

Your explanation is unclear and lacks punctuation. There is no "[product_name] library" as you mentioned. Also, it's not valid to directly compare the memory flags of these two controllers. On [product_name], S7 M0.0 maps to [product_name] M1, S7 M0.1 to [product_name] M2, S7 M0.2 to [product_name] M3, and this mapping continues accordingly. S7 M1.0 corresponds to [product_name] M9, S7 M1.1 to [product_name] M10, and so forth. To read the VM area, you should access it as DB1. For example, S7 DB1.X0.0 maps to [product_name] V0.0, S7 DB1.X0.1 maps to [product_name] V0.1, S7 DB1.DBW0 is [product_name] VW0, and S7 DB1.DBD4 matches [product_name] VD4.
Thank you, that was very helpful.

analysis.insight_summary: The user faced difficulties connecting [product_name] via the [product_name] library, particularly in understanding how memory addresses and variable types correspond between different controllers. Initial expectations were of a simple mapping, but the actual field conversion (for example, M1.0, VM-type variables) did not match those expectations, leading to confusion and problems reading data. Another user provided clarification by outlining correct memory mappings and emphasizing differences in memory conventions between these controllers.
analysis.user_expectations: The user looks for simple and consistent mapping of memory addresses between controllers when using [product_name] with [product_name] library, and also expects straightforward access to VM-type variables.
